verdict: Brown & Brown grew revenue 7% to $1.7B as last year's Accession acquisition added people and premiums, but underlying organic growth was just 1.2% in a soft insurance pricing market.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Total revenue was $1.7B, vs $1.6B a year ago (+7.4%)

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $0.68 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $1.07, +2%

kpis.label: Organic revenue growth
kpis.note: Growth from the existing business, excluding deals

kpis.label: EBITDAC — Adjusted
kpis.note: A 34.6% margin, vs 36.6% a year ago

segments.name: Commissions and fees
segments.note: Commissions from insurers and fees for placing insurance for clients — up 10%, mostly because acquired businesses (above all Accession, bought just over a year ago) are now in the numbers. Organic growth was only 1.2%.

segments.name: Investment and other income
segments.note: Investment and other income — down from $56M a year ago, when the company earned extra interest on cash raised for the Accession deal.

opex.name: Employee compensation & benefits
opex.note: Pay for about 23,000 teammates, including roughly 5,000 who joined with Accession — by far the biggest cost, about half of revenue.

opex.name: Other operating expenses
opex.note: Offices, technology and other day-to-day running costs.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of customer relationships and other intangibles bought in acquisitions — up from $93M as deals pile up.

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: Wear and tear on buildings and equipment.

otherDetail: Costs below operating profit were $113M, net: $100M of interest expense and a $27M increase in what Brown & Brown expects to pay for past acquisitions (earn-out payables), partly offset by a $14M noncash gain on the escrow liability from the Accession deal.
footerNote: Brown & Brown reports no cost-of-revenue line — every cost is an operating or other expense, so gross profit equals revenue. Net income was $241M before $1M attributable to noncontrolling interests; net income attributable to the company was $240M. Operating profit of $433M is revenue less operating expenses (compensation, other operating, amortization and depreciation), before interest and the earn-out and escrow items shown in other expense.
oneTimers: Change in estimated acquisition earn-out payables: a $27M expense — the company raised what it expects to pay sellers of past acquisitions (worth $0.06 of EPS in its adjusted figures).
Acquisition and integration costs of $36M, mainly tied to Accession, excluded from adjusted results.
A $14M noncash gain from marking the Accession escrow liability to market, partly offsetting the items above.
Excluding these items and $110M of amortization, adjusted EPS was $1.07 vs $0.67 GAAP, and EBITDAC — Adjusted was $597M.

takeaways.title: Real growth was slow
takeaways.text: Strip out acquisitions and organic revenue grew just 1.2% (1.5% including contingent commissions) — management called it a challenging rate environment, meaning insurers are cutting the prices that drive Brown & Brown's commissions.

takeaways.title: Deals still drive the headline
takeaways.text: Commissions and fees rose 10% to $1.7B, and nine-month revenue is up 23% — almost all of it bought, led by Accession, which added about 5,000 teammates just over a year ago.

takeaways.title: Margins slipped a little
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDAC margin fell from 36.6% to 34.6% as costs from the bigger, acquired business grew faster than organic revenue, and diluted GAAP EPS dipped to $0.67 from $0.68 because the Accession deal issued more shares.
